info.title: Replay Crate API
info.description: Records every Spotify play, counts plays per track, manages playlists and serves listening metrics. Every error is JSON `{ error: <code>, ...details }`, and every response carries `X-Request-Id`.

post.description: Step 1 of 3. The browser parses the Extended Streaming History export and uploads only timestamp, play time and track (or podcast episode) id: create, add plays and listens (in chunks), finish.
Step 2 of 3. Up to 5000 plays and podcast listens in all per request; call as often as needed. Listens are what the export splits at every pause, already joined.
Step 3 of 3. Plays of known tracks and listens of known episodes move into the history now; unknown ones are queued for lookup and follow. Closes any history gap the import covers.

Answers once the device is playing it (not_started when it doesn't show there in time); not_found when it has left Up next.

index.description: Where it is in Up next (the queue's `queue`), counting from 0.

put.description: Spotify only reaches devices it lists now: one played on before (`isAvailable: false`) fails with not_found until it has Spotify open.

play.description: Start playing there; otherwise keep the current state.

post.description: For the search dashboards in Kibana: a search that led somewhere (a result picked, or all results shown), not every keystroke. Recorded only when search runs on Elasticsearch; otherwise accepted and dropped.

204.description: Recorded, or dropped when there is nowhere to record it.

get.description: Tracks from all of Spotify, for finding music you have never played. Only the free text of `q` is sent (filters are for your library), and Spotify returns at most 10. Separate from /search, so Spotify's latency or rate limits never hold up your library's results.
Shows and episodes from all of Spotify, at most 10 of each, like `/search/spotify` for tracks: only the free text of `q` is sent.

200.description: Shows and episodes, best match first.

get.description: Tracks, artists, albums, playlists and plays in your library, grouped by type, as you type. `q` is free text (typo-tolerant, matched at word starts) plus filters: `artist:` `album:` `in:` (playlist) `from:` (played from) `genre:` `rating:` `plays:` `year:` `played:` `type:`, with comparisons (`rating:>=4`), ranges (`year:1990..1995`), decades (`year:90s`), quotes, and `-` to exclude. `played:` is when you played it: a day, month or year (`2024-09-29`, `2024-09`, `2024`), `>=2025-01`, `2019..2020`, or `today`, `yesterday`, `7d`, `4w`, in the days of `tz`. `genre:` matches whole words of an artist's genres in order (`genre:rock` finds art rock, not rockabilly). Ranked by match, then your plays and ratings.

schema.description: Comma-separated: track, artist, album, playlist, play, show, episode. Default: all.

parameters.description: Comma-separated: track, artist, album, playlist, play, show, episode. Default: all.
parameters.name: types

schema.description: Hits per group.

parameters.description: Hits per group.
parameters.name: limit

schema.description: Hits to skip in each group.

parameters.description: Hits to skip in each group.
parameters.name: offset

schema.description: IANA time zone for `played:` days.

parameters.description: IANA time zone for `played:` days.
parameters.name: tz

get.description: Every genre your played tracks' artists have, most played first. A play counts once for each genre its track's artists have. Genres come from Last.fm tags, else MusicBrainz, and fill in in the background, so recently played artists have them first.

200.description: The genres, with how many of your plays fall in each.

patch.description: Changes the settings given and leaves the rest.

playTracksFrom.description: Where a track played on its own starts from: its album, or the playlist it was last played from (its album when there's none). Up next is the rest of it.
